utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Let me propose the following, that is, that we continue with the agenda I gave yesterday, and perhaps I should give more opportunity to speak to the Defence of Radic because that is our next case. Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have in front of us the reports of expert witnesses for the accused Kvocka [as interpreted]. The Prosecutor agreed to the admission of two reports without cross-examining the witness. In view of Rule 94 bis (C), the Chamber will, therefore, admit the reports as exhibits, as part of the evidence in this case, without calling the witnesses in question to testify before the Bench. So that is one of our rulings. Still regarding the Defence of Mr. Kos, yesterday we resolved the problem, that is, the issue, of protective measures. The witness who was supposed to come and in respect of whom video conferencing was requested, we will organise that at the same time, so we will have an opportunity to hear the witness in that way. The protective measures which were requested in respect of that witness, I think that the Kos Defence still requests these protective measures even in case of videolink. I should like to hear them on this issue, if necessary, at least to confirm what I have just said, and in order to be clear on what kind of protective measures are being sought. Can the Kos Defence please notify the Chamber of that issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Perhaps we should go into closed session to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time do you think you will need?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No more than a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the benefit of the public which is following, as you can see, our proceedings, we will go into a private session for just a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in public session. As regards the request made by the Kos Defence relating to the Detention Unit, we will see to it that the appropriate measures are taken so that the Defence can receive the information requested. The accused Radic, I believe it's a priority, because next week we will be hearing the case in defence of Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said next week. No? The week after. Yes. Thank you. Thank you for drawing my attention to the calendar. Yes, you're quite right. Still pending is the issue of expert witnesses. We have heard the position of the Prosecutor, so I think that it is up to the Chamber to issue its ruling now. I don't know whether the Prosecutor, Ms. Somers, has anything to add to the response. Yes, Ms. Somers, let us hear you. Do you have any good news to tell us?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On the expert witnesses for the Radic Defence, yes, Your Honour, Mr. Fila and I have, as to the witness Kecmanovic's statement, pursuant to the Chamber's urging us to find perhaps a written means of addressing it as opposed to live cross-examination, we have agreed in writing and have submitted a copy to the Chamber just to know about it, that we, as the Prosecution, maintain our non-acceptance. But rather than have cross-examination, we will submit our own expert report in refutation of their report, and hope that that would suit the Chamber's concerns over time, and I think Mr. Fila agrees that that might be as good. On the other two -- the psychiatric reports, we, of course, have not changed our position on. We will seek cross-examination of both experts. And on the report of Mr. Beatovic, Dr. Beatovic, we also would seek to challenge that and cross-examine. But we did try, where we could, reach the accord, which will save a fair amount of time, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Somers. Mr. Fila, do you wish to add something to the issue of expert witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, due to the problems with translation, I agree with Ms. Somers that instead of hearing Professor Kecmanovic, the Prosecution submits their written objections. If that is what has just been stated, then we have an agreement on that, because I have received a somewhat different translation. As regards to other experts - I don't know their names by heart by now - as well as Mr. Beatovic, it is the position of the Defence that there is no need to call them to testify, the reason being judicial economy, not that I would have any special objections to their testifying here in Court. In our system, these testimonies would be considered only in relation to sentencing, and in view of the relevant provision of your Statute, you have an obligation to take into account the practice of sentencing before domestic courts. That is not the case in our system. For example, as regards Ms. Najman, the Chamber ordered that a Dutch expert be appointed, and they managed to find an agreement. As regards Professor Beatovic, again mindful of the judicial economy, I chose him, because in the Kunarac case he was heard as an expert witness. He was examined by the Prosecution and his testimony is on the record. I have nothing against that portion of his -- of the record being made part of the evidence in this case. I do not wish to contest any of that. So that would solve the problem. That was the reason why I elected him as our expert witness, because he has already been used for that purpose and he has already been cross-examined, and things will move faster. If my learned colleague insists on calling them, then I have nothing against it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Fila. Your suggestion is quite welcome. Ms. Somers, do you have anything to say in response to this suggestion of Mr. Fila? He chose one expert witness because he has already testified in another case on more or less the same issue. I view the Office of the Prosecutor as one and single institution. Do you have anything to say in response to this suggestion of Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. I have something to say. Perhaps in the other case the first admission of the psychiatrist was not the one that he made in our case, which was that he did not follow procedure, which suggests that it is a fundamentally-flawed examination, and therefore I would request in this instance, irrespective of what may have taken place in another Chamber, because that apparently was not a concern there, we would have to examine him on his methodology and the procedure, which, by his own admission, was not standard, was not followed. The other psychologist, we have indicated we challenge on the basis -- on a number of bases, among them bias, and would ask the opportunity -- albeit I don't expect to have to extensively cross-examine, nonetheless cross-examination, I think, is appropriate. We have set the grounds out in our response. On Dr. Beatovic -- I'm sorry. Perhaps -- was it Dr. Beatovic? I thought it was a psychiatrist that was referred to in the other case, in Kunarac. I may have misunderstood the use of it. I was referring to Dr. van den Bussche. Perhaps it was a misunderstanding on my part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I thought it was about Professor Beatovic, because you said it was irrelevant. But Mr. Fila suggested that in addition to admitting the report, that we also admit or tender the record of his testimony and the record of his cross-examination. That is what I wanted to hear you on, your opinion on that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, but I hope the Chamber doesn't mind that I did inform it as well as the bases for our wishing to cross-examine the psychiatrist. I think that also should be a matter for the Chamber to know. The statement of Dr. Beatovic, we maintain, is irrelevant, purely irrelevant. However, if the Chamber is going to consider it, we would want to -- even though the Office of the Prosecutor is an integral organisation, there are different aspects of a witness's testimony which may be sought by one Prosecution team in a given case that may vary in another case, and we would ask to have an opportunity as to the points that we think need to be challenged, to have a quick but opportunity to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Somers, I am not going to give you any guidelines for your work, it's not my task here. But in my capacity as a Presiding Judge and a Judge of this Tribunal, we have to balance the objectives and have in mind the resources that we have for that. We really need to know what is the objective of calling one particular witness in view of the overall case. If it is, indeed, very important that we should call him for the purposes of the case, then of course we will call the witness to testify. But I don't need a definite answer at the point, and I think that we can move on with our next issue which is mentioned on the agenda that we gave yesterday. There is a request made by the Radic Defence for certain witnesses to produce medical documents. The issue is under deliberation by the Chamber and we will probably make our ruling shortly. Still regarding our yesterday's agenda, the Zigic Defence, I think we have all of the requests to that effect and they are pending, they are being considered by the Chamber, and we will make a ruling. I think that as far as our yesterday's agenda is concerned we have covered all points, all issues. We received a number of new requests or motions recently, and I should perhaps give the floor to Mr. Fila to argue his motion for protective measures. I don't know whether you need a private session, or do you think you can argue the motion publicly?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I refrain from mentioning the names, I think I can address the issue in public, and the names are not necessary. The witnesses in question are witnesses who have not requested protective measures on a prior occasion, except for the one who is a Serb and who requested safe conduct here and back. However, I must say that there is a leakage of information from this Tribunal. People happened to learn about things, about testimonies, which is then inevitably followed by a number of threats and various kinds of trouble. You will remember the issue which we had in the Blaskic case. All of a sudden, names of witnesses become publicly known. I am absolutely sure that this cannot happen at this level here, at the level of the participants here in the proceedings; however, we should try to find out how such leakages are possible. That is the reason why certain witnesses, all of a sudden, decide to request protective measures. The situation has changed from this past Friday, and that is the subject of my motion. I kindly request the Chamber to grant this request for protective measures because these witnesses have explicitly told me that they would not come here if they are not granted protective measures. They are all non-Serbs, victims who were detained in the camp and who are willing to put a nice word here before the Chamber on behalf of Mr. Radic. That is why they are requesting these protective measures, and these are the grounds for my motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Fila. Before I give the floor to Ms. Somers, I need to ask two questions. When you say that information leaks from this Tribunal, I don't know whether you are referring to public sessions or private sessions. Also, the list which you mentioned, I wanted to know whether it was a confidential list or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really don't know. Yes, it was a confidential document, but I don't know how it became known. We also come to learn the names of Prosecution witnesses, I have to be honest about that; but how such things become known, I really don't know. Whether these people talk in public, in cafes, at home, whether this is due to a lack of conscientiousness on behalf of certain individuals, I don't know. For example, a witness of mine recently received a telephone call on behalf of someone who introduced himself as counsel for the accused Radic and who told him that he didn't need to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say that they talk in cafes, at home, is it here, in The Hague, or over there?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not here, over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Fila. We will see if there is anything we can do about it. Ms. Somers, any comments, reactions, or suggestions in respect of this motion?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On this particular motion, Your Honour, we do not oppose the protective measures, as we know them, that are suggested. Of course, the matter of safe conduct is in the Chamber's hands and is really not for us to comment on. But as to the measures, as long as it's an open session, we think there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Susan Somers. Your reservation was on condition that these hearings be held in public session. What exactly did you mean by "an open session"?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I understand correctly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about protective measures here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Right. And within the context of open session, a pseudonym, distortion, absolutely no problem, no problem at all. Anything else would be in the Chamber's hands. It's not something addressed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber is going to review the matter and make a ruling certainly before you begin your case, Mr. Fila. For the Radic Defence, are there any other questions? I think not. Yes, there are. Documents. But I've already told you that that is under review, so please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there's no problem. I don't want to spoil your week by telling you about my problems. I'll keep them to myself. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, with respect to the Radic Defence, we have no other issues to address. I think that we still have a question which I forgot to mention for the Zigic Defence, and that is the question of a witness that the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Zigic Defence would like to call in his two-fold capacity as a witness of fact and as an expert witness. Could you, Mr. Stojanovic, explain that for us? What is the Rule that you are relying on for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you. I think that we would be saving on time and resources for the Tribunal because this is one of the leading doctors of the general hospital in Prijedor who personally treated Zigic's wounds; that is one point. The second is that one of the leading physicians of that hospital also had insight into the treatment of one of the dead in Keraterm whose death is attributed to our client. This is a person who has the knowledge of an eyewitness, on the one hand, and on the other, he has the expertise of medical knowledge. In our first revised list, we did suggest a medical expert witness. This one would just stand in place of that former medical expert. So he would not be an addition, but instead of the expert Dunjic, we would have this person as the medical expert. So I think that it would be useful and helpful, and it would save time. We have submitted our request to the Registry. They have told us that we should notify the Chamber about it. It is rather important that we have a ruling quickly, because if it be granted, then the expert witness could start working immediately. In any event, this same person has been proposed anyway as an eyewitness and, in our judgement, he will have to come anyway. If I may add, his finding as an expert witness and his statement as an eyewitness do not coincide in every respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovic, for me to be able to understand better what you are telling us, when you say that this expert witness is also a fact witness, the facts that he observed, were they facts that have to do with the observation of a patient or some other facts? In other words, the facts that he observed, are they facts related to a patient of his, of a particular patient?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To make myself quite clear, I can say that it is a physician who personally treated Mr. Zoran Zigic. He amputated his finger, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but why not call him as an expert witness? He observed this and he has his opinion, and that's it, that would be it. That would mean that he would have to produce a report in accordance with Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we accept your suggestion gladly on condition that you make such a ruling. His presence as a fact witness was on our list as a reserve, but we would prefer, in fact, to bring him as an expert witness. If the Chamber were to accept him as an expert witness, he would be deleted from the list of fact witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question for you, Mr. Stojanovic, before I give the floor to Ms. Susan Somers, because there are many things at stake here. We also have your request of the 15th of February for protective measures. Could you give us an idea primarily with respect to the grounds for protective measures and the grounds for a videolink so that we can hear the views of the Prosecutor after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we suggested protective measures for four witnesses, if I'm not mistaken. Four or five -- no, sorry, five. Four of them are of Muslim ethnicity, and they personally feel, as they told us, that they would be at risk if it were to be learnt that they were testifying here for somebody charged for crimes against Muslims. All of them are, today, living in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Also, and this may be more a problem for the Victims and Witnesses Unit, they also requested dislocation. This is something that may be discussed later should the Chamber, by decision, grant such a possibility. The fifth witness is not of Muslim ethnicity. According to his own assurances, he is prepared to mention certain names or certain persons who committed some of the crimes of which Mr. Zigic is charged; however, those persons are at liberty and, as far as we know, in his vicinity. So that is the reason why he has requested protection from public knowledge, that such statements should not become a matter of public knowledge. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But, Mr. Stojanovic, the reasons for the video conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that for one witness, the reason is rather simple. He simply doesn't dare fly, get on an aeroplane. If necessary, we can consult a psychiatrist about this. But if he were not to fly, it would take several days for him to come here and get back again. That is the reason for one witness. For the second, I must say quite openly that he was mentioned on two Tribunal indictments and he does not feel quite safe coming into this courtroom. The former main Prosecutor, Ms. Louise Arbour, withdrew further proceedings against him, but I think if one were to put oneself in his position, one might understand his fears of appearing in this Tribunal. You have his name; there is no secret about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. We need to speed things up a little because we have to finish at 3.00, as I have said. Ms. Susan Somers, these matters that were discussed -- also, I didn't ask Mr. Stojanovic to comment on the motion for the production of documents and manuscripts, that is, the motion of the 13th of February, 2001, and the points having to do with protective measures. So, Ms. Susan Somers, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: As to, Your Honour, the issue of the physician appearing in an expert capacity, we do object. This particular physician is intimately involved, factually, in the defence of the Zigic case. The essence of expert testimony is impartiality, neutrality, objectivity, and I submit to this Trial Chamber it is virtually impossible for this individual to present an objective, impartial, and neutral line of testimony. Therefore, I think the only capacity in which he could appear and submit to full cross-examination that would be meaningful would be as a fact witness. Working slightly backward, a motion for production of documents and manuscripts I don't believe I have seen. Oh, I see. It's on the latter part. I'm sorry. I thought it was a separate document. If I can take a minute and review it, I will certainly look at this. If this in any way is supposed to substitute for 66(B), we'll have to look at that, because that, of course, would have its own very specific language. But let me just look at that in a moment, if I may. On the issue of a witness who was formerly an indictee appearing, that is a matter fully within the control of my counsel opposite. I could only indicate that it was my understanding at the time of withdrawal of indictments that the reasons were not going to issues of probable cause. They had other concerns attached to them. So I cannot address anything other than it is a judgement call by Mr. Stojanovic, and whatever measures he deems appropriate to seek from the Chamber would have to be really in his court to determine. If I -- may I have just a moment to review the request on the documents, and then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on issues of original signatures on documents, I am not clear what document the Prosecutor has in the evidence vault that would indicate whether it is a copy or an original. If I may be permitted to check, I will do that. At this point, I don't know whether it really is literally an original original, or a certified copy. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon has indicated that it's possible that, as this concerns a former witness, perhaps the Witness Unit may have a document with the handwriting sample on it, because of requirements for signing for various aspects of travel reimbursement or travel documents, and that may be an alternative. But I shall check, certainly, and see what the status of our document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is that the Zigic Defence needs signatures to be able to make a comparative study. So to know whether the signature in that document is the real signature, I have to have a document with the real signature that is recognised as a real signature, and that is what the Zigic Defence has asked, if I understood them correctly. I didn't give him the floor about this because I thought you had read the request. In any event, we have a written request and you can respond in writing, and the Chamber will rule. But I have a question for you, Ms. Susan Somers. This question of a doctor who examined the accused Mr. Zigic, whether he should come as an expert witness or a fact witness, you have told us your opinion. But if he comes in his capacity as fact witness, would you admit that, being a physician, that he can also be examined about his opinion and not simply in the strictest sense regarding information? What is your position about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It would depend on what opinion is being called for. Normally treating physicians would indicate: I did A -- the patient came, I did A, B, or C, released the patient with the following instructions. To project into the future would require, I think, quite an establishment of credentials, and I'm not sure that above and beyond what the physician did as a treating physician would be appropriate to inquire into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is a comment rather like the one I make. Everyone is referring to his own system. In my system, if a witness of fact is considered qualified to give an opinion on facts, he can be asked about those opinions. If, for example, a party produces a witness, being a qualified doctor with specialisation possibly, one might agree to ask him about things which are not merely information but which can fall under the category of expertise, opinion, qualifications, and so on. Do you understand my point?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour, and I think that the Chamber does this with witnesses, for example, from the police, asking questions based on -- I hate to call it expertise, but experience, experiential background. And I think that there is a certain latitude that is afforded, but -- one perhaps can't exactly define it, but one knows it when one sees it, has been exceeded, and I would assume that we would be able to make our appropriate objections if the Chamber -- or if the line of questioning, in our judgement, went beyond what would be appropriate. But yes, of course this happens all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor to Mr. Stojanovic now to respond, because I didn't start out with you. So if you could, rather quickly, tell us your opinion, because we have to complete this Status Conference in 12 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be very brief, Your Honours. I think that it is a fact that -- that the fact that this doctor treated Zigic personally is a great advantage for an expert opinion. In any event, we feel that questions that may be addressed to him may be divided into a section relating to the actual injury; and the second part could be his expertise, his assessment of the intensity of pain suffered by Zigic and what his physical capability was after that injury for a certain given period of time. And another subject which is purely within the area of expertise is the characteristics of the injuries of Emsud Bahonjic, a person who succumbed, according to the indictment, to the beatings of Zoran Zigic and who was admitted to that hospital twice during his detention and about which there is the appropriate documentation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have another request from the Kos Defence which coincides, up to a point, with another request of the Zigic Defence and which affects the position of Witness R. We still do not have the response of the Prosecutor. We are aware of the arguments with respect to Zigic. We will now only take Kos, in two or three words, so that the Prosecutor may respond orally and the Chamber may rule very quickly after that. Who would like to speak on behalf of the Kos Defence? Yes, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have very little to add to what Your Honours have before you within the motion. The essence of our request is that this is relevant evidence and there's a basis for admitting it, and we respectfully request that you do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I may simply inform the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, are you able to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I just now received this from the Kos Defence, and if the Chamber would permit us to review it, although I -- my initial reaction is that it flies in the face of the Chamber's ruling about statements, and I cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for interrupting. Would you prefer to respond in writing, Ms. Susan Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If the Chamber would indulge us, I think it would be better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to clean up the table regarding rulings by the Chamber, and that is why I have asked you for your response. I think that's all. Is there anything else on the part of the parties? Yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be a bad time because of the Chamber's time constraints, but at some point there were several exhibits which were raised for admission earlier and just have not been ruled on. Would it be better to tack this onto the end of another hearing? Because there are something like -- about eight, one of which we were minded of yesterday kindly by Mr. Krstan Simic. I can read the numbers out if it would help, and then if the Chamber wishes ... 3/173, 3/174, 3/175, 3/176, 3/177, 3/178, 3/179, and 3/181.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have another seven minutes, more or less. Mr. Simic, does that have to do with you? I think it does. Do you have a position regarding these documents already? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. In fact, I received this filing from Ms. Somers today, and I will respond in writing. But I would like to remind you of something that I omitted to mention and which we consider to be very important. That is the question of affidavits. We have tendered them, as prescribed by the Rules, and we feel that they should be admitted without cross-examination, because we underline that they are a specific type of testimony and that cross-examination should be an extreme exception.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic, we're going to talk about those documents on another occasion, once you have exchanged filings. With regard to affidavits, I think that I said yesterday that this motion was under review, so perhaps this week or next week a ruling will be made. The Chamber said that it would make rulings at the end of each Defence case, but, as you know, the Prosecutor always has seven days after the appearance of each witness. When the Chamber said that it would render its ruling afterwards, it always means after those seven days, that is, seven days after the last day of your case. So you will have your decision in due time. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just confirming that the Chamber has our filed response, that would be it. Your Honours, may I make inquiry very quickly, so that we don't let this go by the board, on the dates for videolink? Just so we can line up all the -- any personnel who may be necessary. If possible, perhaps at the first opportunity when we return from whenever we return from, we could just not let that disappear. I think it's going to be important for timing. Plus, also to have some exhibits sent, perhaps, along if they need to be presented, if they're not terribly visible here, copies of exhibits. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's fine. We have worked well, we have completed our work six minutes ahead of time, and today we didn't mistreat the interpreters. So it's not always that we treat all the interpreters badly. We will stop there. We won't be seeing each other for a long time now, and we will come again on the date that you are familiar with, at 9.20. So I wish you success in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: at 2.56 p.m. 22 23 24 25 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.
